questions.question: The midpoint theorem says the segment joining the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is:
options: Equal to the third side and perpendicular to it
Parallel to the third side and equal to half of it
Equal to twice the third side
Parallel to the longest side only

questions.question: In triangle XYZ, YZ = 30 cm. M is the midpoint of XY and N is the midpoint of XZ. The length of MN is:
Before quoting the midpoint theorem, the question must supply:
options: Midpoints on TWO DIFFERENT sides of the same triangle
Two midpoints on the SAME side
One midpoint and a right angle

questions.question: In triangle XYZ with XY = 18 cm, YZ = 30 cm and XZ = 22 cm, M and N are the midpoints of XY and XZ. The perimeter of triangle XMN is:

subtopics.title: Proving It — Two Copies Make a Parallelogram

questions.question: The construction that opens the standard proof in triangle PQR is:
options: Drop a perpendicular from P to QR
Extend MN to K so that MN = NK, and join KR
Draw the circle through P, Q and R

questions.question: Triangles PMN and RKN are proved congruent by:
options: Side-angle-side, using PN = NR, MN = NK and vertically opposite angles at N

questions.question: MQRK is shown to be a parallelogram because:
options: One pair of opposite sides, MQ and KR, are both equal and parallel

questions.question: Once MQRK is a parallelogram, MK = QR. The final step to MN = ½QR uses the fact that:
options: QR was bisected by the construction
Triangle PMN has half the area
MN and QR are alternate segments
MN is half of MK, because K was constructed so that MN = NK

subtopics.title: The Converse — One Midpoint and a Parallel Line

questions.question: The converse of the midpoint theorem says a line through the midpoint of one side, parallel to a second side:
options: Is perpendicular to the third side

questions.question: In triangle ABC, AB = 16 cm, AP = 8 cm with P on AB, and PQ is parallel to BC with Q on AC. Which conclusion is correct?
options: Q is the midpoint of AC, so PQ = half of BC
Nothing follows, because only one midpoint is given

questions.question: In that triangle, BC = 26 cm. The length of PQ is:
The reason markers expect when you use the converse is:
options: Alternate angles, PQ parallel to BC
Line through midpoint parallel to second side

questions.question: In the rider on triangle KLM with midpoints X, Y and Z of KL, KM and LM, XYZL is proved a parallelogram by aiming at:
options: One pair of opposite sides both equal and parallel

questions.question: In that rider, XY = LZ because:
options: They look equal in the sketch
XYZL is given as a parallelogram
Both equal half of LM — XY by the midpoint theorem, LZ because Z is the midpoint of LM

questions.question: A learner is given MN = 15 cm, where M and N are midpoints of two sides. They write that the third side is 7,5 cm. The error is:
options: Using the converse instead of the theorem
Halving when they should double — the join is the SHORT segment, so the third side is 30 cm

questions.question: Which is a legitimate reason to treat a point as a midpoint in a rider?
options: It looks like the middle of the segment
A ruler shows the halves are roughly equal
The question states it, or the diagram carries matching tick marks on the two halves

questions.question: The brace fixed between the halfway marks on two rafters is:
options: The same length as the base beam
At right angles to the base beam
Parallel to the base beam and exactly half its length

questions.question: If the base beam is 12 metres, the brace across the halfway marks measures:
Reading the roof backwards: the brace measures 4 metres. The base beam is:
In the scissors-and-spin explanation, the small top triangle is given a half-turn about:
options: The halfway mark on one rafter
The middle of the base beam
A corner of the base beam

questions.question: After the spin, the two pieces form a parallelogram. The 'half' comes from the fact that:
options: A parallelogram has four equal sides
Two brace-lengths lie along the top, and a parallelogram's top equals its bottom — the base beam
The brace was measured on site

questions.question: The 'parallel' half of the theorem comes from the same picture because:
options: The rafters are the same length
The carpenter used a spirit level
The top and bottom of a parallelogram always run parallel

questions.question: Joining all THREE middle marks of a triangle produces:
options: Four identical small triangles, each with sides half as long as the original's

questions.question: The theorem's signature in a question is:
options: The word 'midpoint', or matching tick marks, on TWO different sides of one triangle
A right angle in the triangle

questions.question: When you quote the midpoint theorem, the advice is to write down:
options: Both conclusions — the parallel AND the half — even if the question seems to want only one

questions.question: A question gives ONE midpoint and says the line through it is parallel to another side. This is:
options: Enough — that line lands exactly on the middle of the remaining side
A signal to use congruency instead

questions.question: Which reason belongs beside a statement that used two given midpoints?
options: Line through midpoint parallel to second side
